draft.title: Business in the economy
card: businesses employ people and pay them wages. Workers spend that income, which supports other businesses and the jobs they offer.
businesses pay taxes, such as company tax. Governments use this money to fund services such as schools, hospitals and roads.
the goods and services businesses produce add to the economy's total output. More output usually means higher living standards, as people can buy more of what they need and want.
businesses can also lower quality of life. Pollution, noise or traffic from a business can fall on people who live nearby.
draft.remember: Businesses bring jobs, taxes and output, but they can also harm the people around them.

a.q: How does the tax a business pays help the wider community?
opts: It funds services such as public hospitals
It is paid to workers as their wages
It is kept by the owners as a reward
It buys new equipment for the business
a.why: Tax goes to the government, which spends it on services like hospitals, schools and roads. Wages are a separate benefit: they go straight to workers, not through the government.
a.clue: Who receives the tax, and what do they spend it on?

b.q: Jake opens a brickworks near Lithgow. It hires 40 locals, but dust from its kilns settles on nearby homes. Which statement is correct?
opts: It provides incomes but harms quality of life nearby
It provides incomes, so it causes no harm to anyone
It harms quality of life, so it adds nothing to output
It funds services but does not create any local jobs
b.why: The 40 jobs give locals incomes, and the dust harms people living nearby. Both effects happen at once. A business that provides jobs can still lower quality of life, so the benefit does not cancel the harm.
b.clue: Can one business help and harm a community at the same time?

a.best: It funds services such as public hospitals

b.best: It provides incomes but harms quality of life nearby
